subtasks.title: Add DeviceStatus (three-state) to src/core/notifier.rs and a device_status() resolver
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/005_8b95ea464bd9/architecture/notifier_mechanisms.md. is_device_connected() at notifier.rs:216 is pure Tier-1 enumerate (never opens). host_capable() at notifier.rs:689 reads HOST_CAPABLE AtomicBool (line 270), set true by perform_handshake_with at line 558 on a Gain, reset false by reset_handshake_state() at line 706 on a Loss. The status-poll threads (tray.rs:380-406, linux_tray.rs:259-301) already drive handshake_action and keep host_capable() correct on every transition. The simpler enum form { Connected, NoModule, Disconnected } is preferred for P1 (per-board count defers to P3's classify_devices). Spec table: DEVICE_DISCOVERY.md section 3.
2. INPUT: src/core/notifier.rs (is_device_connected at line 216, host_capable at line 689, HOST_CAPABLE at line 270).
3. LOGIC: Add pub enum DeviceStatus { Connected, NoModule, Disconnected }. Add pub fn device_status() -> DeviceStatus deriving per the three-state table: Disconnected = !is_device_connected(); NoModule = is_device_connected() && !host_capable(); Connected = is_device_connected() && host_capable(). Do NOT add per-path pinging here. Keep is_device_connected() unchanged (still used by write-path/broadcast decision and picker Tier-1 pass).
4. OUTPUT: DeviceStatus + device_status() in notifier.rs with unit tests for the three derivations (including the is_device_connected && !host_capable -> NoModule case). No UI change yet (S2/S3 consume this).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the device_status()/DeviceStatus doc-comment to cite DEVICE_DISCOVERY.md section 3 and explain derivation from existing state (so a future reader doesn't assume a per-path ping).

subtasks.title: Render three-state status in src/tray.rs (macOS/Windows)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/005_8b95ea464bd9/architecture/tray_surfaces.md. UserEvent::DeviceStatus(bool) is at tray.rs:41. device_status_text(connected: bool) is at tray.rs:660. The status-poll thread is at tray.rs:380-406 (3s interval, seeds last with startup_device_was_connected(), sends UserEvent::DeviceStatus only on transition). The event-loop arm is at tray.rs:507-510 (calls device_status_i.set_text). First-paint creates MenuItem at tray.rs:312-319 with device_status_text(is_device_connected()) and enabled=false (disabled label). The handshake_action/perform_handshake/reset lifecycle stays keyed on the Tier-1 is_device_connected() transition at lines 390-401 — do NOT gate it on the three-state value. Spec: UI.md section 4 three-state table.
2. INPUT: DeviceStatus + device_status() from P1.M1.T1.S1. spec/UI.md section 4. spec/DEVICE_DISCOVERY.md section 3.
3. LOGIC: Change UserEvent::DeviceStatus(bool) -> UserEvent::DeviceStatus(DeviceStatus). Rewrite device_status_text as fn device_status_text(DeviceStatus) -> String with three branches: (U+25CF solid dot) 'Device Connected' / (U+26A0 warning) 'No module' / (U+25CB hollow circle) 'Disconnected'. The poll thread calls device_status() instead of is_device_connected() for the event payload, but KEEPS is_device_connected() for the handshake lifecycle gating (Gain/Loss at lines 390-401). First-paint at line 316 calls device_status(). The 'No module' warning glyph must remain a disabled MenuItem (parity with today's false arg at line 316).

subtasks.title: Render three-state status in src/linux_tray.rs + the Disconnected->No-module one-shot notify-send
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/005_8b95ea464bd9/architecture/tray_surfaces.md. QmkTray.device_connected: bool is at linux_tray.rs:68. Status-line build is inlined at linux_tray.rs:144-152 (same glyphs as tray.rs). Icon-dim-on-disconnect is at linux_tray.rs:156-169 (dim_icon scales alpha to ~35% via DIM_ALPHA=90 at line 923). Poll thread at linux_tray.rs:259-301 (1s interval, updates via poll_handle.update). The notify helper linux_tray::notify(summary, body) is at linux_tray.rs:846-859 (shells out to notify-send with --app-name=QMKonnect --icon=input-keyboard). notify-rust is deliberately avoided (nested tokio runtime panics in ksni's handler thread, spec section 7.3). The once-guard pattern to mirror is RULES_INVALID_NOTIFIED at notifier.rs:299 (AtomicBool::swap(true, SeqCst) to fire once, store(false, SeqCst) to re-arm). The parity test at linux_tray.rs:948 (status_text_uses_parity_glyphs) must be updated for the new three-state strings. handshake lifecycle stays keyed on the Tier-1 transition at lines 276-288.
2. INPUT: DeviceStatus from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Replace device_connected: bool with a DeviceStatus field on QmkTray. Menu line branches on three states: warning glyph full-alpha for NoModule; hollow circle dimmed for Disconnected; solid circle full-alpha for Connected. Icon-alpha: full-alpha for Connected AND NoModule (device IS present, just not capable); dimmed for Disconnected. The poll thread tracks the previous DeviceStatus and, on a Disconnected->NoModule transition ONLY, fires a one-shot notify-send (guarded so it fires once per entry into NoModule, not every tick — use a new AtomicBool once-guard modeled on RULES_INVALID_NOTIFIED). The handshake lifecycle stays keyed on the Tier-1 is_device_connected() transition. Update the parity test at linux_tray.rs:948.
4. OUTPUT: Linux SNI tray is three-state; the one-shot notification fires exactly once on the transition. cargo test + cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The QmkTray status doc-comment cites DEVICE_DISCOVERY.md section 3 + the one-shot rationale.

tasks.title: Assert R-COEX: non-seize opens, bounded reads, first-byte-0x81 emission
tasks.description: Add R-COEX invariant comments at the open/send sites and invariant tests asserting every constructed report's first payload byte is 0x81.

subtasks.title: Add R-COEX invariant comments at the open sites + invariant tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/005_8b95ea464bd9/architecture/external_deps.md. QMKonnect links hidapi=2.6 (unified to 2.6.6 in Cargo.lock). The crate opens via info.open_device(api) at core.rs:754 — hidapi's DEFAULT non-seize open (FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE Windows, kIOHIDOptionsTypeNone macOS, plain hidraw open Linux). The app does NOT call any seize path; hidapi exposes none. IN_DRAIN_MAX=32 is in the CRATE (core.rs:131), NOT in notifier.rs — the read discipline (pre/post-send bounded drains) is entirely crate-side. The app's send path: QmkNotifier::send_command at notifier.rs:799 builds RunParameters and calls qmk_notifier::run(params). QmkNotifier::notify at notifier.rs:756 builds RunParameters with SendMessage and calls qmk_notifier::run(params). The app's first emitted payload byte is always 0x81 (the magic header). The crate's RunCommand variants (SendMessage, QueryInfo, QueryCallback, SetOs, ApplyHostContext) all construct 0x81-prefixed reports. There is NO per-path send or seize option exposed by the crate.
2. INPUT: src/core/notifier.rs (the QmkNotifier::send_command at line 799 / notify at line 756 transport boundary), spec/DEVICE_DISCOVERY.md section 6, spec/ARCHITECTURE.md section 10 (#10).
3. LOGIC: (a) Add a 'R-COEX — must preserve' doc-comment at the send_command/transport boundary in notifier.rs (near line 799 or the QmkNotifier impl block) stating three rules: never introduce a seize/exclusive open; never a perpetual blocking read; the first payload byte is always 0x81. Add // R-COEX: inline markers at any code that touches the open/send path. (b) Add unit tests asserting that every constructed report's first payload byte is 0x81: construct the SendMessage/ApplyHostContext/QueryInfo framing via the crate's RunCommand and RunParameters, call the app-side builders, and assert the first byte. Where a behavior can't be unit-tested without HID hardware (the non-seize open itself, the bounded-drain discipline), add an inline invariant comment + a // R-COEX: marker.
4. OUTPUT: notifier.rs invariant comments + the 0x81-emission test passing. No runtime behavior change (this phase asserts what's already true).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The invariant comments ARE the Mode-A doc for this phase (they live in code). No docs/*.md change beyond what P4 covers.

subtasks.title: Add DeviceKind / ClassifiedDevice types + CLASSIFICATION_CACHE infrastructure to src/core/notifier.rs
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/005_8b95ea464bd9/architecture/notifier_mechanisms.md and external_deps.md. The crate's CommandResponse::Info{proto_ver:2, feature_flags, callback_count, board_rules_present} variant is the capable classifier (lib.rs). classify_devices will enumerate via hidapi::HidApi::new() (same as is_device_connected at notifier.rs:216 and list_devices at notifier.rs:129), then for each candidate send QUERY_INFO via send_command(RunCommand::QueryInfo, &filter). The existing perform_handshake at notifier.rs:348 already sends QUERY_INFO and sets HOST_CAPABLE — that IS the Tier-2 probe for the global status. CLASSIFICATION_CACHE should be a Mutex<HashMap<String,(DeviceKind,Instant)>> keyed by device path, with CLASSIFICATION_TTL default 5s. The crate's MatchKey (core.rs:641) is filter-keyed NOT path-keyed, so per-candidate classification requires narrowing the filter to the candidate's vid/pid (the only mechanism available app-side).
2. INPUT: src/core/notifier.rs (existing types, DeviceFilter at line 83, configured_filter at line 95, send_command path via Notifier trait at line 56).
3. LOGIC: Add pub enum DeviceKind { Capable { proto_ver: u8, feature_flags: u8, callback_count: u8, board_rules_present: bool }, NotQmkNotifier }. Add pub struct ClassifiedDevice { path: String, vendor_id: u16, product_id: u16, product_name: Option<String>, usage_page: u16, usage: u16, kind: DeviceKind }. Add const CLASSIFICATION_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5). Add static CLASSIFICATION_CACHE: Lazy<Mutex<HashMap<String, (DeviceKind, std::time::Instant)>>> keyed by path. Add helper fn classification_cache_get(path) / fn classification_cache_insert(path, kind) / fn classification_cache_clear(). No classify_devices() logic yet (that's S2).
4. OUTPUT: DeviceKind, ClassifiedDevice, CLASSIFICATION_CACHE + helpers in notifier.rs. Compiles. No logic yet.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] DeviceKind/ClassifiedDevice/CLASSIFICATION_CACHE doc-comments cite DEVICE_DISCOVERY.md section 2.

subtasks.title: Implement classify_devices() logic + unit tests with mock HID layer
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/005_8b95ea464bd9/architecture/notifier_mechanisms.md and external_deps.md. list_devices() at notifier.rs:129 enumerates via hidapi::HidApi. The handshake (perform_handshake_with at line 421) sends QUERY_INFO via n.send_command(RunCommand::QueryInfo, &filter) at line 436 and matches CommandResponse::Info{proto_ver:2} for capable. send_command takes a DeviceFilter (vid/pid/page/usage), not a path, and the crate opens ALL matches. Per-candidate ping mechanism: narrow the filter to the candidate's vid/pid (only viable when vid/pid is unique on the bus — document this limitation). The MockNotifier at notifier.rs:1278 records calls and returns queued CommandResponse values; set_notifier at line 903 injects the mock. Mock setup pattern: reset_test_state(); reset_handshake_state(); set_notifier(Box::new(MockNotifier::new())); set_mock_responses(vec![...]). Tests MUST run single-threaded (--test-threads=1).
2. INPUT: DeviceKind/ClassifiedDevice/CLASSIFICATION_CACHE from P3.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement pub fn classify_devices(verbose: bool) -> Vec<ClassifiedDevice>: enumerate Tier-1 candidates via HidApi::new() (usage_page==0xFF60 && usage==0x61 + optional vid/pid). For each candidate: check CLASSIFICATION_CACHE for a fresh entry (within TTL); if cached, use it; otherwise, narrow a DeviceFilter to the candidate's vid/pid and call get_notifier().lock().send_command(RunCommand::QueryInfo, &narrowed_filter). Match the CommandResponse: Info{proto_ver:2} -> Capable{...}; Timeout/Legacy/anything-else -> NotQmkNotifier. Insert result into CLASSIFICATION_CACHE. Also feed the cache from the existing perform_handshake path (so the status path stays single-ping-per-appearance). Invalidate cache entries on device disappearance (path no longer in enumerate). Document the multi-same-vid/pid limitation in a comment. No board is harmed (VIA ignores magic).
4. OUTPUT: classify_devices() + cache integration in notifier.rs, with unit tests over the MockNotifier (capable/legacy/timeout -> correct DeviceKind; cache hit/miss/TTL). The mock infra may need a small extension to return per-device responses — extend MOCK_RESPONSES to be FIFO-queued per send_command call (already is).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] classify_devices doc-comment cites DEVICE_DISCOVERY.md section 2 and records the per-candidate mechanism chosen (filter-narrow-by-vid/pid) + its limitation.
